Kill-a-stupid-rule movement and exposure of legacy rules
Campaign reward for surfacing rules and whack-a-mole elimination

sections.description: Opening framing: three actions to think about for hardwiring believing in your organization’s core competency.
sections.title: Introduction: Three actions to hardwire belief

sections.description: Revamp how you hire by starting with core values and incorporating values-based screening as the initial step, with Chick-fil-A mentioned as an example.
sections.title: Action 1 — Hire with core values

sections.description: Introduce a campaign to surface and discard outdated rules. Legacy rules that once made sense become counterproductive; reward exposure of these rules and celebrate their removal with the team, described through the 'kill-a-stupid rule' movement and 'whack-a-mole' elimination approach.
sections.title: Action 2 — Kill-a-stupid-rule movement and elimination of legacy rules

sections.description: Finish with financial transparency: share your financials with every employee to build trust; cites Container Store as an example of a privately held company sharing full financial reports with all staff.
sections.title: Action 3 — Share financials with employees

summary: Jeanne Bliss presents three concrete actions to hardwire belief in an organization's core competency: first, revamp hiring by starting with core values and adopting values-based screening (citing Chick-fil-A as an example); second, launch a “kill-a-stupid rule” movement to expose and eliminate outdated legacy rules, rewarding transparency and even celebrating successful removals with employee engagement; and third, share financials with all employees to build trust, with Container Store cited as an example of open financial reporting within a private company.
title: Three Actions to Build a Culture of Belief in Your Organization
topics: Commerce Bank origin of the rule movement
